112	### 2. Wrap the element
113	
114	When `event.scaffold` is present, the helper already found the source and computed the wrapper; treat it as the successful output and skip the command. `event.scaffoldAttempted` with `scaffoldError` means preflight could not finish; use the command below.
115	
116	**On source-preview targets `event.scaffold` carries `sourceWritten: false`.** The helper did NOT write the wrapper; it hands you `scaffold.wrapperBlock` plus the picked element's source range (`replaceStartLine`, `replaceEndLine`, 1-indexed). Write the wrapper **and** all variants in ONE edit: splice your variants into `wrapperBlock` at the "Variants: insert below this line" marker, then replace lines `[replaceStartLine, replaceEndLine]` with the result. A separate scaffold write reloads the framework before your variant write lands and strands the browser at 0/N. (`replaceEndLine < replaceStartLine` means insert mode: insert, remove nothing.) The `svelte-component` path never sets `sourceWritten`.
117	
118	```bash
119	"<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable" live-wrap --id EVENT_ID --count EVENT_COUNT --element-id "ELEMENT_ID" --classes "class1,class2" --tag "div" --text "TEXT_SNIPPET"
120	```
121	
122	Flag mapping (keep separate, never collapse into `--query`): `--element-id` ← `event.element.id`; `--classes` ← classes joined with commas; `--tag` ← tagName; `--text` ← first ~80 chars of textContent, **every call**: it disambiguates repeated sibling components, and without it a class locator lands on the first match. If `event.pageUrl` implies the file, pass `--file PATH`. If `--text` still matches several candidates, wrap exits `{ error: "element_ambiguous", candidates, fallback: "agent-driven" }`: pick the right range from page context and write the wrapper manually per the fallback flow.
123	
124	An element with neither an id nor classes (a bare `<h1>`, the usual first pick on a fresh page) leaves both flags out; the tag alone locates it:
125	
126	```bash
127	"<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable" live-wrap --id EVENT_ID --count EVENT_COUNT --tag "h1" --text "TEXT_SNIPPET"
128	```
129	
130	A tag alone never lands on the first match: when the tag repeats and `--text` does not single out one element, or the element shares a source line with other markup (`reason: "shared_line"`), wrap exits `element_ambiguous`; follow the fallback flow as above. Short text settles it only when it is one element's whole text.
131	
132	Success output: `{ file, insertLine, commentSyntax, styleMode, styleTag, cssSelectorPrefixExamples, cssAuthoring }` (plus the `sourceWritten: false` fields above on source-preview targets). Run directly with no preflight scaffold, it writes the wrapper itself and you splice variants at `insertLine`. `styleMode` controls how preview CSS must be authored. Treat it as a detected capability mode, not a framework guess: `scoped` means `@scope ([data-impeccable-variant="N"])` rules; `astro-global-prefixed` means explicit `[data-impeccable-variant="N"]` prefixes with the exact returned `styleTag`. Use `cssAuthoring` as the source of truth for the current file (styleTag, selector strategy, requirements, forbidden patterns); apply no framework-specific exception unless it says to.
133	
134	For Svelte/SvelteKit targets, `impeccable live-wrap` returns `previewMode: "svelte-component"` with `file` pointing at a temporary `node_modules/.impeccable-live/<id>/manifest.json`, `componentDir` holding the variant components, and `sourceFile` the real route. The scaffold is AST-based: control-flow blocks (`{#each}`, `{#if}`) survive intact and a free each-collection crosses the contract as ONE structured prop (kind `collection`). The payload includes `componentStubMarkup` (the prop-substituted markup already written into every stub), so do not read the manifest or stubs back. EDIT `v1.svelte`, `v2.svelte`, ... in place; never delete and recreate them; keep the stub's control flow and `propContract` prop names; never flatten a loop into literal items. The stub `<style>` arrives seeded with the source rules that currently style the selection; restyle or delete them freely. On accept, any seeded rule your variant does not re-declare is REMOVED from the source (the preview never applied it, so the user approved a design without it). Use semantic class selectors, no `@scope`, no `data-impeccable-*`. Reply with `--file` set to the manifest path; the browser mounts the compiled components so Svelte HMR does not reset page state. Accept merges the chosen component back mechanically (markup restored to route expressions, CSS reconciled, params baked, indentation preserved); you have no post-accept cleanup on this path. When the selection contains constructs a detached preview cannot support (component tags, `bind:`/`use:`, await blocks, inline scripts, spread attributes), wrap returns the normal source-preview wrapper with `previewFallback: { from: "svelte-component", reason }`; just follow the returned shape.
135	
136	**Params on component-preview paths go in a sidecar, never as an attribute** (Svelte parses `{` in attribute values as an expression). Declare them in `componentDir/params.json` keyed by variant number, using the schema from section 7:
137	
138	```json
139	{ "1": [ {"id":"density","kind":"steps","default":"snug","label":"Density","options":[
140	    {"value":"airy","label":"Airy"},{"value":"snug","label":"Snug"} ]} ] }
141	```
142	
143	Author the component `<style>` against `var(--p-<id>, default)` for `range`/`toggle` and `[data-p-<id>="…"]` for `steps`, wrapped in `:global(...)` so runtime knob values on the mounted root reach your rules.
144	
145	**Fallback errors.** Wrap refuses to write into non-source files (generated, untracked): accepting into one is silent data loss. Three shapes, all with `fallback: "agent-driven"` (see **Handle fallback**): `file_is_generated` (your `--file` points at a generated file), `element_not_in_source` with `generatedMatch` (element only exists generated), `element_not_found` (likely runtime-injected).
146	
147	### 3. Load the action's reference
148	
149	`event.action` is `impeccable` (freeform): work from SKILL.md's design rules plus [craft-floor.md](craft-floor.md); decide the visitor mode from the surface; do not load a sub-command reference. Freeform is not a pass to skip parameters: follow the budget and freeform bias in section 7. Any other action (`bolder`, `quieter`, `distill`, `polish`, `typeset`, `colorize`, `layout`, `adapt`, `animate`, `delight`, `overdrive`): read `reference/<action>.md` before planning; its MUST params layer on top of the section 7 budget.
150	
151	### 4. Plan three variants: identity first, then mode, then axes
152	
153	Live runs on an existing surface; the brand is already chosen. The job is variation **within identity**, not selection between identities. The worst failure is three off-brand variants the user cannot accept. Four phases, in order.
154	
155	#### Phase A: Extract the identity (non-skippable)
156	
157	Sources in priority order: DESIGN.md's visual system fields; CSS custom properties (de-facto tokens); computed styles on the picked element and parent; sibling components' visual rhetoric. Write ONE sentence recording what is actually on screen: dominant surface and accent color (real values, not "warm"), the loaded font pairing, layout topology (stacked / side-by-side / grid / asymmetric / overlay), surface treatment (corners, borders, shadows, decoration density), and the voice tone read off the copy. Be specific; skip an axis rather than fabricate; do not name an aesthetic family (a conclusion, not data). This sentence is the **identity lock**: every variant must read as the same brand side by side. Absence of DESIGN.md is never an excuse.
158	
159	#### Phase B: Pick mode (default vs departure)
160	
161	**Default** preserves the identity and varies expression within it; right for ~90% of sessions. **Departure** rejects the identity; trigger ONLY on the user's explicit ask in the current request or prompt ("redesign this", "rebuild from scratch", "something completely different"); a stale critique or old note is not authorization. Unsure means default: wrong-default costs "three on-brand variants with similar feel" (recoverable), wrong-departure costs three off-brand variants (unrecoverable).
162	
163	#### Phase C: Plan three variants
164	
165	**Default mode.** Each variant commits to a different **primary axis**, preserving the identity sentence. The six axes: 1 **Hierarchy** (which element commands the eye), 2 **Layout topology** (stacked / side-by-side / grid / asymmetric / overlay), 3 **Typographic system** (pairing logic, scale ratio, case/weight, *within the available faces*), 4 **Color strategy** (which existing palette role carries the surface: Restrained / Committed / Full palette / Drenched; existing tokens only), 5 **Density** (minimal / comfortable / dense), 6 **Structural decomposition** (merge, split, progressive disclosure). Three variants, three DIFFERENT axes: the same brand at three angles. New fonts, new hues, or new aesthetic-family signals belong to departure mode only.
166	
167	**Departure mode.** Each variant anchors to a different aesthetic direction derived from the brand, never a fixed catalog: read PRODUCT.md's Brand Personality words; derive physical, spatial, or material experiences that embody them; from those, derive three directions genuinely different from each other AND from the current surface; reject reflex choices whose rationale would fit a neighboring product. Each direction must be one concrete sentence naming a real-world referent ("a museum exhibition label system", not "clean and minimal").
168	
169	**In both modes, name each variant's 2 or 3 parameter knobs while planning** (section 7 budget). Parameters are part of the design; deciding "what's tunable" during planning beats retrofitting.
170	
171	#### Phase D: Squint test
172	
173	**Default:** compare each variant against the Phase A lock; palette, type voice, or rhetoric drift means it crossed into departure by accident: rework. Then confirm three different primary axes; three "tighter density" variants is failure. **Departure:** two passes, family before sentence. Family pass (non-negotiable): label each variant with a concrete family of your own choosing; shared or interchangeable labels mean rework. Sentence pass: three one-line descriptions side by side; two that rhyme mean rework. When the primary axis is color or theme, the trio must not share theme + dominant hue: three color worlds, not three shades.
174	
175	**Action-specific invocations** must vary along the action's dimension; in default mode every variation stays within the available faces and existing tokens:
176	
177	- `bolder`: amplify a different dimension per variant (scale / saturation / structural change).
178	- `quieter`: pull back a different dimension (color / ornament / spacing).
179	- `distill`: remove a different class of excess (visual noise / redundant content / nested structure).
180	- `polish`: a different refinement axis (rhythm / hierarchy / micro-details).
181	- `typeset`: departure varies the pairing AND the scale ratio each; default keeps the faces and varies scale ratio, case, and weight each.
182	- `colorize`: departure gives each a different hue family and varies chroma and contrast strategy; default gives each a different existing palette role carrying the surface (Restrained / Committed / Full palette / Drenched) and a different contrast strategy.
183	- `layout`: different structural arrangement, not spacing tweaks.
184	- `adapt`: different target context per variant (mobile-first / tablet / desktop / print or low-data).
185	- `animate`: different motion vocabulary (cascade stagger / clip wipe / scale-and-focus / morph / parallax).
186	- `delight`: different flavor of personality (micro-interaction / typographic surprise / illustrated accent / sonic-or-haptic / easter egg).
187	- `overdrive`: different convention broken (scale / structure / motion / input model / state transitions); skip its "propose and ask" step, live is non-interactive.
188	
189	### 5. Apply the freeform prompt (if present)
190	
191	`event.freeformPrompt` is the user's ceiling on direction: all variants honor it while exploring different interpretations within the Phase B mode. Default mode: the prompt narrows the axes, not the identity ("more confident" → one variant amplifies hierarchy, one commits the accent color, one tightens density). Departure mode: the prompt narrows the lanes, not the families ("newspaper front page" → broadsheet vs tabloid vs trade journal, then run the family pass). When the prompt conflicts with a binding brand commitment or DESIGN.md invariant, preserve the invariant unless the user explicitly revokes it.
192	
193	### 6. Deliver variants
194	
195	Complete HTML replacement of the original element per variant, not a CSS-only patch. Colocate preview CSS as a `<style>` tag inside the wrapper. **Atomic default:** CSS + all variants + parameter manifests in one edit at `insertLine`.
196	
197	```html
198	<!-- Variants: insert below this line -->
199	<style data-impeccable-css="SESSION_ID">
200	  /* rules matching cssAuthoring.rulePattern */
201	</style>
202	<div data-impeccable-variant="1">
203	  <!-- variant 1: full element replacement (single top-level element) -->
204	</div>
205	<div data-impeccable-variant="2" style="display: none">
206	  <!-- variant 2 -->
207	</div>
208	<div data-impeccable-variant="3" style="display: none">
209	  <!-- variant 3 -->
210	</div>
211	```
212	
213	Replace the style opening tag with `cssAuthoring.styleTag` when the tool returns a different one, and close it with `cssAuthoring.styleClose` (`</component>` on `.vue`). **Each variant div contains exactly one top-level element**, same tag as the original; loose siblings break outline tracking and accept. First variant visible, all others `display: none`. The browser's MutationObserver accepts atomic or progressive arrival; accepting an arrived variant fences the worker, so later publications are rejected.
214	
215	For `styleMode: "scoped"`, author every `:scope` rule with a descendant combinator: the `@scope` boundary is the variant wrapper div, not your element, so a bare `:scope { ... }` styles a `display: contents` shell. Always step in (`:scope > .card`, `:scope .hero-title`). The fake test agent's CSS in the [repo agent template](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/blob/8dac6ae7e020c43ab10ce9b41939f6fd42627b96/tests/live-e2e/agent.mjs) is a faithful template.
216	
217	**JSX / TSX targets:** wrap `<style>` content in a template literal (CSS braces would parse as JSX), use `className=` / `style={{…}}`, keep `data-impeccable-*` attributes as plain strings:
218	
219	```tsx
220	<style data-impeccable-css="SESSION_ID">{`
221	  @scope ([data-impeccable-variant="1"]) { ... }
222	`}</style>
223	<div data-impeccable-variant="2" style={{ display: 'none' }}>
224	  {/* variant 2 */}
225	</div>
226	```
227	
228	The wrap script provides a single-rooted JSX wrapper with the marker comments inside; drop the block at the marker and the source stays valid TSX.
229	
230	### 7. Parameters (composition-sized, 0-4 per variant)
231	
232	Each variant can expose **coarse** knobs; the browser docks one control per parameter with zero regeneration cost (knobs drive a CSS variable or data attribute your scoped CSS is authored against). Wire an axis as soon as the user could plausibly mutter "a bit tighter" or "a touch more accent" without wanting a regeneration; micro-margins and one-off nudges are not parameters. Freeform bias: you chose the axes, so expose them; a hero with 0 params is almost always a mistake, and 1 is underweight unless the design is a genuine fixed point.
233	
234	Budget scales with the element's VISUAL weight (count visual children, not DOM depth):
235	
236	- **Leaf / tiny** (button, icon, bare heading): **0 params.**
237	- **Small composition** (simple card, labeled input, ≤ ~5 visual children): **0-1**.
238	- **Medium composition** (section, nav cluster, 6-15 children): **target 2**; 1 if simple.
239	- **Large composition** (hero, full region, 16+ children or sub-sections): **target 2-3, up to 4** when independent axes are all authored in CSS.
240	
241	**Hard cap: four** per variant. For named sub-commands, the action reference's MUST params are non-negotiable when expressible; respect the cap, no duplicate knobs.
242	
243	**Declare** on the HTML/JSX path as a wrapper attribute (component-preview paths use `componentDir/params.json` instead, same schema, keyed by variant number; see the wrap section):
244	
245	```html
246	<div data-impeccable-variant="1" data-impeccable-params='[
247	  {"id":"color-amount","kind":"range","min":0,"max":1,"step":0.05,"default":0.5,"label":"Color amount"},
248	  {"id":"serif","kind":"toggle","default":false,"label":"Serif display"}
249	]'>
250	```
251	
252	Three kinds: `range` (slider; drives `--p-<id>`; author `var(--p-color-amount, 0.5)`; fields min/max/step/default/label), `steps` (segmented radio; drives `data-p-<id>`; author `:scope[data-p-density="airy"] .grid { ... }`; fields options/default/label), `toggle` (drives both `--p-<id>: 0|1` and attribute presence; fields default/label). Reset on variant switch is a known limitation: each variant starts at its declared defaults.
253	
254	**On accept**, the browser sends current values and `impeccable live-accept` writes them as a sibling comment: `<!-- impeccable-param-values SESSION_ID: {"color-amount":0.7} -->`. Carbonize cleanup bakes them: keep only the matching `steps`/`toggle` branch, drop the others, collapse `:scope[data-p-…]` to semantic rules; substitute `range` literals or update the var's default.
255	
256	### 8. Signal done
257	
258	```bash
259	"<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable" live-poll --reply EVENT_ID done --file RELATIVE_PATH
260	```
261	
262	`RELATIVE_PATH` is relative to project root; the browser fetches source directly if the dev server lacks HMR. Then poll again immediately.
263	
264	### Aborting an in-flight session
265	
266	If wrap or generation fails after the browser flipped to GENERATING, tell the **browser** so its bar resets: `"<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable" live-poll --reply EVENT_ID error "Short reason"`. Never use `live-accept --discard` for this (pure file mutator, browser never sees it, bar sticks on dots); `--discard` is only source-side cleanup for a discard the browser itself initiated.
267	
268	## Handle fallback
269	
270	When wrap returns `fallback: "agent-driven"`, you pick the source file yourself; the goal is unchanged: three preview variants now, and the accepted one persisted where the next build cannot wipe it.
271	
272	1. **Find where the element really lives** from the error payload: `element_not_in_source` + `generatedMatch` means the served HTML is generated, so find the generator's template or partial; `element_not_found` means runtime-injected, so find the rendering component or data source; `file_is_generated` resolves the same way. A purely visual change may belong in a shared stylesheet rather than a template.
273	2. **Preview in the served file**: manually write the same wrapper scaffold `impeccable live-wrap` produces into the file the browser actually loaded, moving the element itself into the original slot: `<!-- impeccable-variants-start ID --><div data-impeccable-variants="ID" data-impeccable-variant-count="3" style="display: contents"><div data-impeccable-variant="original">THE ELEMENT, UNCHANGED</div><!-- Variants: insert below this line --></div><!-- impeccable-variants-end ID -->`. Insert your variant divs after the marker, then `--reply EVENT_ID done --file <served file>`. Put the start marker and the end marker each on a line of its own: accept replaces whole lines from marker to marker, so a marker that shares its line with other markup takes that markup with it (in a one-line or minified file, break the line around the element first). Never drop the original slot: discard restores the element from it and refuses a wrapper without one. This edit is temporary; a regen wiping it is fine.
274	3. **On accept, write to true source** (accept refuses generated files, so `_acceptResult.handled` is usually `false` here): structural change → template/component source; visual-only → the right stylesheet; content rendered from data → the data source or render logic. Then remove the temporary wrapper from the served file.
275	4. **On discard**, just remove the temporary wrapper.
276	
277	## Handle `accept`
278	
279	Event: `{id, variantId, _acceptResult, _completionAck}`. The poll script already ran `impeccable live-accept` deterministically and acknowledged delivery; the browser DOM is already updated.
280	
281	- The accept event includes `pageUrl`; the poll script must forward it to `impeccable live-accept --page-url PAGE_URL` so accept-time cleanup only scrubs staged copy edits for the current page.
282	- `_completionAck.ok !== true`: do not poll yet. Run `impeccable live-status` / `impeccable live-resume`, finish cleanup manually if needed, then `impeccable live-complete --id EVENT_ID`.
283	- `handled: true, carbonize: false`: nothing to do; poll again.
284	- `handled: true, carbonize: true`: required cleanup below; `_acceptResult.todo`, `_completionAck.requiresComplete`, and the stderr banner all point at it.
285	- `handled: false, mode: "fallback"`: the session lived in a generated file; you already wrote true source in fallback Step 3; clean the temporary wrapper and poll.
286	- `handled: false, mode: "error"`: **do not hand-edit the file**, with one exception. `source_locked`: rerun the same `impeccable live-accept` command (idempotent) until the publisher releases. `markers_share_line`: a session marker comment shares its line with other markup and nothing was written; move each marker onto a line of its own (the only edit allowed), then rerun the same command. `accept_receipt_conflict`: the session already resolved as `priorOperation`; run `impeccable live-status` and tell the user. Anything else: report briefly, run `impeccable live-status` first.
287	- `handled: false` without `mode`: manual cleanup: read file, find markers, edit.
288	
289	### Required after accept (carbonize)
290	
291	`carbonize: true` means the accepted variant is stitched into source with helper markers and inline CSS (so the browser renders with no gap). That stitch-in is temporary; rewrite it into permanent form before anything else, or dead `@scope` rules, wrapper divs, and marker comments accumulate across sessions. Five steps, synchronously, before the next poll:
292	
293	1. **Locate the carbonize block** in `_acceptResult.file`: the `<!-- impeccable-carbonize-start/end SESSION_ID -->` markers bracket only the `data-impeccable-css` style element, and the accepted `data-impeccable-variant` div follows the end marker (on JSX both sit inside an outer `data-impeccable-carbonize` div). `SESSION_ID` here, in `styleTag` and in every `--id` is the event's `id`; read the `<!-- impeccable-param-values -->` comment first when present, it drives steps 3 and 4.
294	2. **Move the CSS rules** into the project's real stylesheet (whichever already owns styling for the surrounding element).
295	3. **Bake param values while rewriting selectors**: retarget `@scope ([data-impeccable-variant="N"])` to real semantic classes; keep only the `:scope[data-p-<id>="VALUE"]` branch matching the chosen value; substitute `var(--p-<id>)` literals or update the var's default.
296	4. **Unwrap the accepted content**: delete the inner variant div (and on JSX the outer `data-impeccable-carbonize` div); drop `data-impeccable-params` and all `data-p-*` attributes.
297	5. **Delete** the inline `data-impeccable-css` style element, the param-values comment, both carbonize markers, and any `@scope` rules for non-accepted variants.
298	
299	Then run `impeccable live-complete --id SESSION_ID` and verify `phase: "completed"` before polling again. The command is a gate, not a formality: it refuses with `error: "source_dirty"` plus findings while any live-mode leftover remains; fix and rerun (`--force` only for false positives).
300	
301	## Handle `discard`
302	
303	Event: `{id, _acceptResult, _completionAck}`. The poll script already restored the original and acknowledged `discarded`. Nothing to do unless `_completionAck.ok !== true`; then `impeccable live-complete --id EVENT_ID --discarded` and poll again.
304	
305	## Handle `steer`
306	
307	Event: `{id, message, pageUrl}`: page-level direction from the global bar's Steer control (typed or spoken), no element context, no variant cycling. Read `message`, inspect the page or files as needed, make edits or answer in prose. Reply `"<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable" live-poll --reply EVENT_ID steer_done ["Optional short toast"]`, or on failure `--reply EVENT_ID error "Short reason"`, then poll immediately. No separate pickup reply; the Steer bar unlocks on `steer_done` or `error`.
308	
309	## Handle `prefetch`
310	
311	Event: `{pageUrl}`: fired once per route on first selection; the user is likely about to Go on a page you have not read. Resolve the route to its file (root `/` is usually the boot's `pageFile`; multi-page sites often map `/foo` to `public/foo/index.html`; SPAs map everything to one entry), read it, poll again. No `--reply`. If you cannot resolve it confidently, skip and poll.
312	
313	## Handle `manual_edit_apply`
314	
315	Event: `{id, pageUrl, batch: {entries}, evidencePath?, chunk?, repair?, deadlineMs}`.
316	
317	The user already clicked Apply. Do not ask what to do, discard, or redirect to Go. The parent live thread keeps the foreground poll loop and sends the final `/poll --reply --data`.
318	
319	When native subagents are available, delegate source edits to `impeccable_manual_edit_applier` / `impeccable-manual-edit-applier`. Pass cwd, scripts path, event id, page URL, chunk/deadline, `batch`, `evidencePath`, and the canonical JSON result schema. The subagent must not poll or reply. If unavailable, apply inline with the same contract.
320	
321	An op with `deleted: true` and `removeElement: true` is the browser's Remove badge: delete that whole element from source, children included, not just its text. Locate it by `sourceHint`, then by `leaf.outerHTML` and `originalText`, and remove exactly that element's source range; leave no empty wrapper, orphaned children, or dangling markup behind.
322	
323	If `repair` is present, the previous Apply changed source but final validation failed. Fix the current source and return the same canonical JSON result; do not roll files back yourself. The browser will ask the user before any rollback.
324	
325	After source edits finish, reply exactly once with `"<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable" live-poll --reply EVENT_ID done --data '{"status":"done","appliedEntryIds":["8hexid"],"failed":[],"files":["src/page.html"],"notes":[]}'`. Use `status:"partial"` or `status:"error"` with `failed[]` when not every entry applied. Then poll again. Never reply without the event id; `--reply done --file ...` is invalid for manual Apply.
326	
327	## Exit
328	
329	The user stops live mode by saying so in chat, closing the tab (SSE drops; poll returns `exit` after 8s), or the browser's exit button. On `exit`, kill any still-running background poll, then clean up.
330	
331	## Cleanup
332	
333	```bash
334	"<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable" live-server stop
335	```
336	
337	Stops the helper and runs `impeccable live-inject --remove` to strip the injected script (use `stop --keep-inject` to keep it for a quick restart; `.impeccable/live/config.json` persists as project config). Then search for and remove any leftover `impeccable-variants-start` wrappers and `impeccable-carbonize-start` blocks, stop a dev server this session started (by its own process id), and when the boot's context asked for the detector (`MANUAL_DETECTOR_REQUIRED`), run it once over the files an accept changed.
338	
339	## First-time setup
340	
341	Only when `impeccable live` reports `config_missing` / `config_invalid`, or `configDrift` needs explaining, or the config lacks `cspChecked`: read [live-setup.md](live-setup.md). It owns the config schema, the per-framework `files` table, injection adapters, drift healing, and the CSP detection and consent flow.
342

One-time live-mode project setup. Loaded from [live.md](live.md) only when `impeccable live` reports `config_missing` / `config_invalid`, when `configDrift` needs handling, or when the config lacks `cspChecked`. Not part of the per-session hot path.

## Write the config

Create the file at the `path` the boot reported (default `.impeccable/live/config.json`):

```json
{
  "files": ["<path-or-glob>", "<path-or-glob>", ...],
  "exclude": ["<optional-glob>", ...],
  "insertBefore": "</body>",
  "commentSyntax": "html",
  "cspChecked": true
}
```

`files` is the inject target: **the HTML files the browser actually loads**, not necessarily source (tracked vs generated does not matter here; wrap has its own generated-file guard). Entries are literal paths or globs. `exclude` (optional) skips files a `files` glob would otherwise include (email templates, demo fixtures). `cspChecked` records that the CSP step below has run; absent on first setup.

**Hard-excluded paths (cannot be overridden):** `**/node_modules/**` and `**/.git/**`; injecting there would instrument third-party code.

**Glob syntax:** `**` matches any number of segments (including zero), `*` matches within a segment, `?` matches one character. Paths are project-root-relative with forward slashes.

| Framework | `files` | `insertBefore` | `commentSyntax` |
|-----------|---------|----------------|-----------------|
| SPA with single shell (Vite / React / Plain HTML) | `["index.html"]` | `</body>` | `html` |
| Next.js (App Router) | `["app/layout.tsx"]` | `</body>` | `jsx` |
| Next.js (Pages) | `["pages/_document.tsx"]` | `</body>` | `jsx` |
| Nuxt | `["app.vue"]` | `</body>` | `html` |
| Svelte / SvelteKit | `["src/app.html"]` | `</body>` | `html` |
| TanStack Router (SPA, Vite) | `["index.html"]` | `</body>` | `html` |
| TanStack Start (SSR) | `["src/routes/__root.tsx"]` | `<Scripts` | `jsx` |
| Astro | `[" <root layout .astro>"]` | `</body>` | `html` |
| Multi-page (separate HTML per route) | `["public/**/*.html"]` glob over the served dir | `</body>` | `html` |

Pick an anchor that exists in every file (`</body>` almost always works); `insertAfter` matches after a line instead. For multi-page sites prefer a glob so new pages are picked up automatically. For sites whose pages are rebuilt by a generator, the inject survives only until the next regeneration: re-run `impeccable live` after each build (accept is unaffected; it writes true source via the fallback flow).

**Framework adapters (auto-detected at inject time).** Every inject records what it wrote in `.impeccable/live/inject-journal.json`; the next inject or remove heals artifacts a crash or wrong-directory stop left behind. SvelteKit, Nuxt, and TanStack Start server-render their document shell, so a raw `<script>` in the entry template will not execute reliably; `impeccable live-inject` detects them and routes to a dedicated adapter (SvelteKit: dev-only root component from `+layout.svelte`; Nuxt: dev-only `.client.ts` plugin; TanStack Start: a generated dev-only `ImpeccableLiveRoot` component in `__root`). The `files` value stays a valid detection/CSP hint but is not the literal insertion site. A plain TanStack Router SPA takes the baseline Vite path.

## Config drift

On every boot the project is scanned for HTML files under common page roots (`public/`, `src/`, `app/`, `pages/`) that the resolved `files` list does not cover; they surface as `configDrift.orphans` with a hint. Tell the user once per session which files are uncovered and offer to add them or switch `files` to a glob. Never auto-update the config; the user decides. `configDrift` is `null` when there is no drift.

## CSP detection (first-time only)

Keep all allowances below development-only, including manual middleware and meta-tag edits. Do not change a deployed production site's CSP to load the localhost helper; see [live.md](live.md) for production inspection alternatives.

If `config.cspChecked === true`, skip this whole section; the user was already asked once.

```bash
"<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable" detect-csp
```

Output `{ shape, signals }`; the shape names the *patch mechanism*, so one template covers many frameworks:

- **`null`**: no CSP; write the config with `cspChecked: true` and stop here.
- **`append-arrays`**: CSP as structured directive arrays; auto-patchable (monorepo helpers with `additionalScriptSrc`/`additionalConnectSrc`, SvelteKit `kit.csp.directives`, Nuxt `nuxt-security`).
- **`append-string`**: CSP as a literal value string; auto-patchable (inline `next.config.*` `headers()`, Nuxt `routeRules`).
- **`middleware`** / **`meta-tag`**: detected but not auto-patched. Show the user the detected files, ask them to add `http://localhost:8400` to `script-src` and `connect-src` manually, then mark `cspChecked: true` and proceed.

### Consent prompt (use this phrasing)

> **CSP patch needed.** I detected a Content Security Policy in your project that blocks `http://localhost:8400`: the live picker won't load without an allowance. Here's the change I'd make:
>
> ```diff
> [file: <patchTarget>]
> [exact diff, 2-5 lines]
> ```
>
> It's guarded by `NODE_ENV === "development"` so the extra entry only appears in dev and never reaches production. You can remove it any time by reverting this file. Apply? [y/n]

On "no": skip the patch, note that live will not work until the allowance is added manually, and still write `cspChecked: true` (the question has been asked). On "yes": apply the shape's patch below, then write `cspChecked: true`. The helper's port is not known until the first successful boot, so the allowance names 8400, the helper's first choice; if that boot then reports a different `serverPort` (another project's helper held 8400), add that port to the same allowance before picking.

### append-arrays

Declare near the top of the file that holds the CSP arrays, then append `...__impeccableLiveDev` to the script-src and connect-src arrays:

```ts
// Dev-only allowance so impeccable live mode can load. Guarded by NODE_ENV.
const __impeccableLiveDev =
  process.env.NODE_ENV === "development" ? ["http://localhost:8400"] : [];
```

Per-framework: Next.js + monorepo helper: edit the *app's* `next.config.*` (not the shared helper), appending to `additionalScriptSrc` / `additionalConnectSrc`. SvelteKit: `svelte.config.js`, `kit.csp.directives['script-src']` and `['connect-src']`. Nuxt + nuxt-security: `nuxt.config.*`, `security.headers.contentSecurityPolicy['script-src']` and `['connect-src']`. Reference outputs: [nextjs-turborepo/expected-after-patch.ts](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/blob/8dac6ae7e020c43ab10ce9b41939f6fd42627b96/tests/framework-fixtures/nextjs-turborepo/expected-after-patch.ts), [sveltekit-csp/expected-after-patch.js](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/blob/8dac6ae7e020c43ab10ce9b41939f6fd42627b96/tests/framework-fixtures/sveltekit-csp/expected-after-patch.js). Idempotency: if `__impeccableLiveDev` already exists in the file, the patch is applied; just mark `cspChecked: true`.

### append-string

Two-point patch: declare a dev-only string, interpolate it into the CSP value at both directives (leading space so it concatenates cleanly; convert literals to template strings as part of the edit):

```ts
// Dev-only allowance so impeccable live mode can load.
const __impeccableLiveDev =
  process.env.NODE_ENV === "development" ? " http://localhost:8400" : "";
```

- `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` becomes `` `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'${__impeccableLiveDev}` ``
- `connect-src 'self'` becomes `` `connect-src 'self'${__impeccableLiveDev}` ``

Per-framework: Next.js inline `headers()` in `next.config.*`; Nuxt `routeRules['/**'].headers['Content-Security-Policy']` in `nuxt.config.*`. Reference outputs: [nextjs-inline-csp/expected-after-patch.js](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/blob/8dac6ae7e020c43ab10ce9b41939f6fd42627b96/tests/framework-fixtures/nextjs-inline-csp/expected-after-patch.js), [nuxt-csp/expected-after-patch.ts](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/blob/8dac6ae7e020c43ab10ce9b41939f6fd42627b96/tests/framework-fixtures/nuxt-csp/expected-after-patch.ts).

## Troubleshooting

If the user said "no" to the CSP patch and later reports live not working: their dev CSP blocks `http://localhost:8400`. Delete `cspChecked` from `.impeccable/live/config.json` and re-run `impeccable live`; setup asks again.

After setup, re-run `impeccable live`.

Build the website a good company would ship: it says plainly what is sold, shows the real thing on
every screen, and looks made for this client, not from a template and not like an art piece.
figma.com and x.ai are the bar (in words: `layout-v4.md` section 1).

`<skill>` is this folder. It needs Node 22+ and Chrome, Edge or Chromium (ffmpeg optional).

## House rules

These nine win over everything else in this skill.

1. **No caption or description under any image, render or visual.** Licence credits go in one
   footer line.
2. **Every visual renders, never an empty ground,** at 1440, 1024, 768 and 390.
3. **One section per screen:** the hero alone on the first screen, every section exactly one or
   two screens tall at 1440x900, no second section heading peeking in. The one exception is a
   live `photo-chapters` section, three or four screens, set by the moment.
4. **Equal left and right content edges.**
5. **Hover micro-animations:** a linked card lifts 2px, a photo zooms 1.02-1.03 inside its frame,
   buttons step on hover and press on click, underlines draw, card loops cycle in 2.5-4 s, repeat
   and restart on hover. The motion layer does it; never strip or override it. No tilt, carousels
   or timed tabs. Every hero enters once on load (`data-enter`), and every page carries one dealt
   moment, two on a long page (the gate holds both).
6. **More and better real photographs where they fit;** nicer backgrounds; better heroes, layouts
   and fonts.
7. **Real full-colour icons** (a known product's real icon, never a drawn one); small diagram
   visuals in cards (a hub with branches; one input, a main processor, three parallel lanes;
   pulses running along the lines).
8. **The big award-site scenes and creative moments are part of the skill:** every page deals its
   moments (photo- and type-led off tech), but shader effects and scenes only where the trade has a
   technical subject (tech, AI, developer tools, gaming, fintech, hardware), never on a local cafe,
   bakery, guesthouse or shop: those get photographs.
9. **Addresses:** street and district only (no street given: the district), no house number, postcode or coordinates; no register
   or VAT numbers; no phone in a real format; contacts on `.example`.

## 1. The kind of business decides everything

Write the kind on the plan's first line and declare it on the page: the page type on
`<html data-type>` and `<meta name="page-type">` (the same value), and `<meta name="site-kind">`;
a place adds `<meta name="page-kind" content="place">`. The dealers take the last column
(`start.mjs --page`, `moments.mjs --page`), the hero dealer the page type; `consistency.mjs` reads
the metas.

| Brief | page type | site-kind | kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| App, SaaS, AI, developer tool, fintech or banking app, a studio selling its own software | software | software | software |
| A game, a studio launching its game | software | gaming | gaming |
| Hardware or a tech device (a drone, a robot arm, a keyboard) | product | tech | tech |
| Any other physical product or brand (a chair, a bike, coffee beans sold online) | product | other | product |
| People are hired: clinic, law firm, agency, creative studio, trade | service | other | service |
| People come to it: cafe, bar, bakery, restaurant, guesthouse, small hotel, shop, florist, bike shop, gym, local studio | place | other | place |

A maker that also opens its door or teaches (a ceramics studio, a bakery with a web shop) is a
**place**; its web shop becomes the goods section. It is a product only when nothing happens at the door.

"Tech" below means site-kind software, gaming or tech; "other" is everything else. Effects,
scenes, loops, counts, CSS grounds, dark pages and dark heroes are tech only. An other page is
photographs, flat colour, type, real icons, the hero's entrance, its dealt moment (photo- or
type-led, `moments.md`) and the hover layer.

## 2. The page plan by kind

The full plans, deal lists and section order: `references/sections.md`.

- **Place** (a cafe, bakery, guesthouse, shop). Photographs lead: 12 to 20 on the full page, 8 to
  12 compact, under 8 frames the 3-screen short page, whatever the trade; no client photographs:
  the draft path and a live search (`photos.md`), then count; the palette dealt by trade. The hero
  a photograph whenever a frame fits (a remote place: its region's landscape), the visit block on
  screen two, the offer, the place, orders or booking.
  **Variety without effects** (`sections.md` section 4): the offer and the place deal different
  compositions, never two sections round one picture; one type moment (the address or name set large); one main action a screen; list text 16px. Flat grounds, square
  photographs, one button style, the phone bar, the dealt moments; no effect, ground, loop,
  fragment, diagram or tab.
- **Product and service** (site-kind other). Photographs lead: the product, the people, the rooms,
  the work, two or more a screen on a product page. Real icons for the tools a studio uses; one
  still diagram at most; flat grounds and one brand band. No shader effect, print, grain, gradient,
  scene or loop (the dealt moments only); WebGL only for a product render the brief asks for. **A
  physical product with no photographs is shown in photographs:** stand-ins of the same kind of
  thing from `photos.mjs search`, each listed in the report, on the full product page; a render
  (`assets/objects/product-render`, stills) only when the brief asks for 3D or a render; never a
  drawing, mood stock or a set of props (`sections.md`, Product).
- **Every product page** (photographed, in stand-ins or rendered on a 3D ask, hardware too; the bar is Figure and 1X;
  `sections.md`, Product): the product **big** where it stands
  whole (most of its frame, or on the ground at anchor scale), never mid-size in a grey rounded
  panel on a grey ground; **a different picture each section**, never one view twice; **every headline promise pictured** (a family bike shows the child bench); dealt
  compositions, no structure twice, one contrasting ground; the **swatch changes the picture**,
  every colour shown once; **no fact twice**; buttons step and press (rule 5).
- **Tech** (software, gaming, hardware). The client's own subject leads at true size. Software: its
  own UI as live HTML showing what it works on (a code-review tool: a red and green diff with its
  Accept action) in one `app-frame`, never a generic dashboard or only fragments on panels; cards:
  fragments on lit panels, pulsing diagrams, real icons. Hardware: its photographs, else stand-in
  photographs of its kind (a render only when the brief asks for 3D), never a split hero of only
  an order form or a drawn SVG. A game: its name in the h1, a launch line, its world as full-bleed
  key art (else its name set large over stand-in photographs of its setting), an effect never in
  its place (`sections.md`, Gaming). **60 to 80 words a screen** outside UI mocks (`copy.md`). By
  deal: **one effect** (a shader ground in the hero or the one `[data-visual]` frame, a WebGL
  part, an object or one big scene) and **one or two moments** in their own sections; four live
  WebGL contexts at most; no card moves with the scroll (`effects-usage.md`).
- **One object never carries the page.** The product or hero object whole leads the hero and **two more sections at
  most**; another kind of visual the brief supports carries the rest (`sections.md` section 1,
  its table): a game's world and crew; hardware's use at the bench, its parts close up; a still
  diagram card, a type moment, a context photograph where the trade allows.
- **The client's own assets get slots.** A trailer, key art, screenshots, CAD renders or a motion
  video the brief names each get a frame that reads finished now (a real `<video>` with a stand-in
  poster, a play control only when there is a page or file to play, three to five stand-in
  photographs of the world, a CAD frame), named in a comment for the client's file, never empty
  (`sections-library.md`, client-slots).

## 4. The run

0. **The stack.** An empty folder builds a static page: copy `<skill>/assets` into `assets` and
   start from `assets/starter.html`. An existing project builds in its own stack, its components
   taking the starter's markup and classes, with the kit copied into its public folder
   (`public/assets`) and loaded from there as plain files. A brief that asks for Next.js builds a
   static export (`output: 'export'`), checked on its built page (`--root out`).

1. **Read the brief.** Write down the kind (section 1), what is sold, who buys it, the one main
   action (the transaction: Book a room, Order a cake, Start a free trial; a place with neither:
   Get directions) and the real material: logo, screens, photographs, prices, address, hours.
   Then arm the finish gate, before any page exists:

   ```bash
   node <skill>/scripts/gate.mjs --start index.html --kind <kind> --category "<what is sold>" --primary "<main action>"
   ```

   A framework build names its dev server's URL (`--start http://localhost:5173/`) or its built page
   (`--start dist/index.html --root dist`; a Next.js export: `out`) in place of `index.html`, and
   rebuilds before every gate run.

2. **Write all the copy first,** with the copy layer (`copy-voice.md`: the fact sheet, the voice
   card on the plan, the page's shape, the device budget; a register from `copy-registers.md`, the
   moves of `copy-moves.md`) within the rules of `copy.md`: the h1 names the category and the buyer or the place (a game: its name and genre),
   one hard fact on the first screen, a noun in every heading, buttons as a verb and an object.
   Nothing is invented but a coined brand name (searched first, the result kept in `names.json`
   beside the page) and, on a place, plausible hours and prices, each marked `data-assumed`
   (`copy.md`, What may be assumed). A draft kept in a `.md` file lints the same way as the page
   (the voice card and part labels are skipped).

3. **Plan the page as screens.** Line 1: the kind. Line 2: the deal (step 4), with one sentence on
   why the palette fits the trade. Then one line per
   section: its id, its one idea, its picture and its kind (object, use, parts, world, slot, diagram, type; three object lines at most), its
   screens (1 or 2, from its content height, `layout-v4.md` section 2), which section holds a
   moment and why it moves (on tech also the effect or the scene). Pick the photographs now (`photos.md`); their count,
   stand-ins included, sets a place's length (section 2). Then read `cards.md` and the recipe of
   every id you use in `sections-library.md`.

4. **Deal, never choose by taste.** Each command keeps a history, so pages differ:

   ```bash
   node <skill>/assets/layout/deal.mjs --type <page type> --has <photo,ui,film,object,setting> --history .taste-skill/layout-history.json   # the hero; a game adds --kind gaming, hardware --kind tech
   node <skill>/scripts/start.mjs deal --page <kind> --trade <trade> --history .taste-skill/history.json    # three palettes made for the trade, three pairings: take the first; add --axis after a word or editorial hero
   node <skill>/scripts/start.mjs css --page <kind> --palette <id> --type <id> --radius soft --history .taste-skill/history.json
   node <skill>/scripts/start.mjs brand --page place --bg "#.." --ink "#.." --accent "#.." [--surface "#.."] [--muted "#.."] --type <id> --radius soft   # the client's own colours (a logo, a painted shopfront), in place of css
   node <skill>/scripts/moments.mjs pick --page <kind> --count 1|2 --fits section,statement --photo --history .taste-skill/history.json   # every kind
   node -e "for(const l of process.argv.slice(1)){const o=l.split('|');console.log(o[Math.floor(Math.random()*o.length)])}" <the kind's lists, below>
   ```

   Run every command from the project folder (the deal arms the gate in the folder it runs in, or
   joins the build already open one or two folders up). The
   lists, in order nav, footer, close, rhythm, buttons, mark (`sections.md` sections 2 and 3):
   - software: `"nav-mega|nav-cards|nav-centre" "footer-dark|footer-statement|footer-columns" "close-type|close-word" "dark-band|surface-pairs|space" "solid|pill|tonal|arrow" "wordmark|initial|arc|ring|stack|dots"`
   - gaming: `"nav-mega|nav-centre|nav-cards" "footer-dark|footer-statement" "close-word|close-type" "dark-band|media-band|space" "solid|pill|block" "wordmark|initial|arc|ring|stack|dots"`
   - product and hardware: `"nav-cards|nav-split|nav-mega" "footer-columns|footer-dark" "close-photo|close-type|close-word" "dark-band|brand-band" "arrow|solid|block|pill" "wordmark|initial|arc|ring|stack|dots"`
   - service: `"nav-mega|nav-split|nav-centre" "footer-visit|footer-dark|footer-columns" "close-type|close-photo" "surface-pairs|dark-band|space" "solid|tonal|block|arrow" "wordmark|initial|arc|ring|stack|dots"`
   - place: the whole line in `sections.md` section 4, Place (The deal), read in its order.

   A product or hardware with no photographs deals with `--has photo` for its stand-ins;
   `--has object` only for a cut-out or a render the brief asks for (always the `product` hero, its
   widest view across the wrap, no box); a game without art files passes `--has setting` (the
   `photo` hero, its name over a stand-in of its setting; a game always passes `--has`). A product
   page is dealt only the product, photo and film heroes. A place's hero is printed, never dealt (`--type
   place`). A dealt part that needs a photograph the page lacks is dealt again (`sections.md` section 2). Take the
   first palette and the first pairing printed (the next only when the first clashes with the
   client's own logo or photographs, or the pairing fails `hero-lines`, said on plan line 2); the client's own colours go through
   `start.mjs brand` instead (`sections.md` section 4, Look); never violet: deal again. Keep the `:root` block as printed. Radius: `sharp` for fintech and developer tools, `soft` by default,
   `round` for consumer apps, square on a place. On tech only: the lit ground (`<html data-ground>`:
   `sand|sky|sage` through the one-liner), the CSS grounds (`backgrounds.md`) and the one effect
   (`effects-usage.md`). Write every result on plan line 2 and in
   the comment at the top of `<body>`, and build exactly that (a short page drops what it has no section for: `sections.md` section 4).

5. **Build.** In `starter.html`: set `<html lang data-type data-radius data-buttons data-motion>`
   (lang: the brief's language), the three metas, the head block (title, description, og, icon,
   theme-color: `system.md`, Head) and the nav class; keep the skip link and the `m-enter` head
   line; copy only the `<section class="hero …" data-enter>` of
   `assets/layout/hero-<id>.html` (never its nav, other sections, footer or credit line; every word
   and picture becomes the client's); move the dealt close and footer out of their `<template>`s
   and delete the rest. Every section is `main > section` with
   one `.wrap`, its h2 first, `--h: 1` or `2`. Build each to its recipe with the system's classes
   and tokens; write page CSS only where a reference says page CSS (inside a visual, `--p-h`,
   `.wall`, `.rail`, `.device`). Paste UI from `assets/ui/<name>/fragment.html` and rewrite every
   name, number and logo to the client's (kit icons become `data-icon`, `cards.md`); a diagram card is `data-diagram="<preset>"`
   with the client's labels; run `icons.mjs scan index.html --out assets/icons --colour` last, so every icon
   the page names is a local file. Mount an effect, object, moment or scene exactly as its
   reference says, never from your own script. A moment's section is copied from
   `assets/moments/_demo/in-page.html` (place: photo-chapters, word-highlight) or
   `in-page-service.html` (pinned-chapters, picture-develops film); a moment's own `demo.html` shows
   it alone and is not a page model. A form is the starter's `booking-form` (`system.md`,
   Forms). Credits: the one footer line from `photos.mjs credits`, once the markup uses the
   photographs (it reads the page). Copy the hero's tile from `shoot.mjs` beside the page as `share.jpg`.

6. **Check and look.** Only the skill's scripts, each running one headless Chrome with WebGL on the
   CPU, closed by its own PID, one at a time in the foreground with a 10-minute timeout; never in
   the background, a windowed browser or a browser tool.
   Each serves the page file itself over http on 127.0.0.1 (never `file://`), so no server is needed;
   for a built page whose links start at the site root (`/_astro/page.css`), pass `--root` with the build folder (`dist`).
   `--profile <dir>` is the Chrome profile: a folder of its own in the OS temp folder or in the
   project's `.taste-skill` folder (`.taste-skill/chrome-check`), never outside the project (no
   `../`); a relative one that leads out of it is replaced by `.taste-skill/chrome-<script>`. Then:

   ```bash
   node <skill>/scripts/copy-lint.mjs index.html --kind <kind>
   node <skill>/scripts/consistency.mjs index.html --widths 1440,1024,820,768,390 --rhythm-widths 1440,820,768,390 --profile <dir> --page <kind> --category "<what is sold>" --primary "<main action>"
   node <skill>/assets/layout/check.mjs --url index.html --profile <dir> --sizes 1440x900,1024x768,820x1180,768x1024,390x844 --shots shots/layout
   node <skill>/scripts/shoot.mjs --url index.html --w 1440 --out shots/1440.png --profile <dir>
   node <skill>/scripts/perf.mjs index.html --profile <dir>
   ```

   Shoot 1024, 820x1180, 768x1024 and 390 as well. Every `check.mjs` finding fails the page (no `--no-stress`).
   copy-lint opens no browser and takes under a second. Fix every FAIL (a copy-lint WARN too, or say
   why it stays) and read the copy aloud (`copy-voice.md` section 6); shoot again and read every
   screenshot against the checklist. In the fix rounds run `consistency.mjs --quick --widths
   1440,390`. Then the gate, which runs the checker at 1440 and 390 every time, walks the page at 320
   for overflow, collide and tap-size, and runs copy-lint, whose FAILs block like the checker's:

   ```bash
   node <skill>/scripts/gate.mjs index.html
   ```

   Fix what it lists and run it again until its last line is `GATE: PASS` or `GATE: OPEN`, three
   rounds at most (in Claude Code it also runs when you finish; a stop before your first gate run is
   no round, and to ask the user something after a block, just stop again). When the user tells you
   to stop, or to ship the page as it is, run `gate.mjs --done "<what they said>"` (`GATE: DONE`)
   and report the open FAILs.
   `GATE: SETUP` (no page yet, a framework's source shell, a page that is not local): arm what a
   browser can open (step 1) and run it again. `GATE: ERROR` (the checks could not run) or
   `GATE: OFF`: put the line in the report and finish; do not rerun. Never edit
   the kit's files or hide anything from the checker. A FAIL you judge false is waived in
   `.taste-skill/waivers.json` with its reason, never fixed by gaming the check (`references/gate.md`);
   a word from the client's own copy that copy-lint FAILs is waived hit by hit, the brief as the reason
   (a word inside the client's name, as the logo or the title writes it, is not counted: one WARN).

7. **Report:** the `GATE:` line first, then every waiver with its reason and every open FAIL; the
   kind, the deal (palette and why it fits, pairing, hero, grounds, effect, moments, scene); the
   voice card in one line and every copy-lint WARN kept, with why; the checker, layout and perf
   results; what you could not check; every assumed fact (the checker's `assumed` list) and the
   coined name's search; the form's `.example` stand-in and the canonical domain still to come; the photographs and art the client must supply, every
   stand-in frame among them (library and live search); every client slot, its file and its stand-in.

## 5. Checklist

Each line names its checks: `consistency.mjs` ids in brackets, `check.mjs` findings in braces,
`perf.mjs` rows. The last line is for your eyes.

- **First screen:** says what is sold, for whom or where, with one hard fact [copy-headline,
  copy-fact]; the hero fills it alone at every width, its main button inside it [hero-screen,
  hero-fill, fold-action, fold-cut] {hero-fold}.
- **One section per screen:** every section 1 or 2 screens, its h2 first and top-aligned, no
  neighbour's heading or picture in its tile, nothing sparse, no section half empty [section-height, one-section,
  one-heading, section-air, one-screen, section-gaps, empty-area] {screen-short, screen-height, sparse,
  neighbour, neighbour-ground}.
- **Equal edges:** every block on the `.wrap` lines or the grid's columns, nothing out to one side,
  no sideways scroll [container-edges, row-lines, split-pair, off-grid, right-edge, col-edge,
  spill, off-viewport, stagger, top-stagger] {edge-left, edge-right, spill, bleed-one-side,
  one-sided, lines}.
- **Every visual draws** at 1440, 1024, 768 and 390; a refused effect shows its still fallback
  [visual-empty, empty-visual, gl-fallback, shader-lint, no-visual, photo-weight].
- **No caption** explains, apologises for or labels a picture; credits in one footer line
  [visual-caption, caption, credit-wall, photo-credit]; no placeholder, sample note or printed
  `.example` address [placeholder, sample-label].
- **The right things for the kind:** outside tech no effect ground, print or scene, only the
  dealt photo- or type-led moments (WebGL only for a product render the brief asked for)
  [effect-kind, effects-fit, photo-print]; the subject itself
  shows: the product big, whole in three sections at most, a new picture each [product-shown,

  real photographs where they fit, none twice [photo-set, photo-repeat, photo-upscale]; real icons in their own

- **Motion:** every button, link, linked card and linked photograph visibly answers the pointer,

  width, a full-screen menu; the place action bar.
- **Your eyes:** beside the figma.com and x.ai frames it reads as a professional company site;
  nothing tilted, staggered, cut or overlapping; the hero is the work, not a mood.

## 6. Never

- A card, row or tile that fades in on scroll; a fade-in on every section; parallax on text;
  scroll-jacking; random blinking.
- Stock photographs passed off as the client's product, people or place (a stand-in is listed in
  the report as one, never shown with another maker's name or logo); a product page that never
  shows the product.
- A drawn look-alike of a real logo; invented reviews, quotes, customers or figures.
- Violet or lavender in the page's own design: accent, ground, gradient, effect colour or tint (a
  real third-party logo keeps its own colours, `icons.md`).
- Copying a reference site's code, copy, pictures or signature effect.
- Deleting or editing the kit's own files (`assets/`, `scripts/`) to clear a check: a check that
  flags a kit file is reported, and the page is checked again after any change.

All in `references/`; section 3 names the one each asset needs.

1	# Copy voice
2	
3	The copy layer. `copy.md` holds the rules every page keeps: the five rules, the contacts, nothing
4	invented. This file decides what the words say and how they sound, so two pages for two clients never
5	read like one writer. Read it at step 2, before the first sentence; `copy-tells.md` and
6	`scripts/copy-lint.mjs` check the result at step 6. The other three files: `copy-moves.md` (the move for
7	each part of the page), `copy-registers.md` (the voices to choose from), `copy-tells.md` (what gives
8	model copy away).
9	
10	## Why model copy reads as model copy
11	
12	The old slop is mostly gone: no "elevate", no "seamless", few em dashes. The new slop looks like good
13	copy, used the same way on every page:
14	
15	- **One voice for every client:** warm, wry, modest, a little literary, mildly against big companies. A
16	  CI tool and a yoga studio sound alike.
17	- **The same devices in every section:** a strip of three invented figures, headings in two fragments
18	  ("Short menu. Long list of regulars."), "X, not Y", "No X. No Y.", a dry joke closing each paragraph, a
19	  pun signing off the footer.
20	- **Sincerity said instead of shown:** honest, calm, quiet, actually, simply, carefully.
21	- **Detail invented to look specific:** a batch number, a minute of the morning, a percentage nobody
22	  measured, and the same few names (Priya, Okafor, Fieldnote) on unrelated sites.
23	
24	Professional copy uses the same devices. What separates it is five things: its details are **true**
25	(and often a little inconvenient); each device is used **once**, where it lands hardest; every brand has
26	its **own voice**; it takes **risks** (it names an enemy, admits a limit); and its pages are **uneven**,
27	leaving out what has nothing true to say. The cause underneath is missing input: with no facts, a model
28	fills a template with plausible inventions. **The fix is facts and decisions, never synonyms.** A word
29	swapped for its synonym is the next tell.
30	
31	## 1. The fact sheet, from the brief
32	
33	Before a sentence, write down what the brief, the client's files or an existing site give, word for
34	word where you can. Each field feeds a part of the page:
35	
36	| Field | What it holds | Where it goes |
37	| --- | --- | --- |
38	| What it is | One plain sentence, no adjective | the h1 and the sub-line |
39	| For whom, and not for whom | The best-fit buyer; who should look elsewhere | the h1 or sub-line, one line in the FAQ |
40	| What they do today instead | A spreadsheet, the big rival, the bakery across town, nothing | the pain line, the comparison |
41	| The true difference | What is true here and not elsewhere, with its proof | the claims worth a heading |
42	| Customer words | Phrases from reviews, emails, the brief's own quotes | the pain line, headings |
43	| Numbers | Each with where it came from | sentences, the facts strip |
44	| People | Names and roles the brief gives | the about block, a quote |
45	| Odd true details | History, an object, a ritual, a house word, the awkward bit | the texture you would otherwise invent |
46	| A limit | What it does not do, who it is wrong for, what is closed | one admission a page |
47	| An enemy | A habit or a category ("re-typing invoices"), never the reader | the pain line, one section |
48	| The offer | Price, trial, booking terms, the one action | buttons, the close |
49	
50	- **Nothing is invented** beyond what `copy.md` allows (a coined name; on a place, plausible hours and
51	  prices). An empty field stays empty: its section shrinks or goes, and the report lists what the client
52	  must supply. Never a `[NEED]`, a bracket or a "coming soon" on the page.
53	- **A thin brief is no reason to stop:** write the best page the facts allow. Only when a person is in
54	  the conversation and asks for copy (not a build) ask at most six questions in one message, most useful
55	  first: who switched to you from what, and why; the one number you would bet on; the objection you hear
56	  most; what you are bad at or not for; a strange true detail of how you work; three real customer
57	  messages.
58	- **A limit and an enemy come from the brief or from plain facts of the trade** ("closed Mondays",
59	  "Mac only", "no lift; rooms on three floors" when the brief says so). An invented flaw is still an
60	  invention.
61	
62	## 2. The voice card
63	
64	**The default voice is out** unless the client asks for it: warm, wry, modest, slightly literary,
65	ending paragraphs on a deadpan twist and saying honest, calm or quiet about itself. It is not bad; it is
66	what every model writes now, and readers know it.
67	
68	Pick one register from `copy-registers.md` by the buyer, the price and the client's real character.
69	When the brief does not settle it, take the one least like the last page this session wrote. Write the
70	card on the plan (step 3), never on the page:
71	
72	```
73	Voice: technical-dry (copy-registers.md 2)
74	Pairs: exact, not cold; sure, not loud; dry only in the empty state
75	Person: "you" for what the buyer gets, "we" for the work; the product is the subject in feature lines
76	Sentences: mostly 8 to 16 words; one long one a section, where it explains
77	Humour: none in the hero, the prices or the FAQ
78	House words: the brief's own nouns (shifts, rota, cover), the same word every time
79	Never: virtue words about ourselves, a pun on the name, a strip of claims
80	```
81	
82	- **Copy the client's own voice first.** A writing sample, an old site or the brief's wording overrides
83	  the menu (never the five rules or the integrity rules).
84	- **Nine other trades:** picture this voice on nine businesses in nine other trades. If it suits any of
85	  them, push it further toward this client.
86	- **Voice holds, tone moves.** The hero and the story carry the most voice. Prices, the FAQ, booking and
87	  forms go plain: readers there are anxious. Errors and confirmations are short and kind.
88	- **The register never bends copy.md's rules:** the h1 still names the category, every heading still has
89	  its noun, every button is still a verb and an object (`copy.md`). Voice lives in which facts you pick,
90	  the sentence shapes, the admission and the microcopy.
91	
92	## 3. Shape from the reader's questions
93	
94	A reader asks, roughly in this order: what is this, is it for me, why believe you, how does it work,
95	what does it cost, what if it goes wrong, what do I do now. How much they already know sets the start:
96	
97	- **They do not know they have the problem:** open the sub-line on a moment they recognise.
98	- **They know the problem:** name it in the customer's words, then the product.
99	- **They are comparing:** lead with the mechanism, what this does differently.
100	- **They know the client:** the product, the offer, the price, the action.
101	
102	- **A section exists only if the brief has true material for it.** Five full sections beat eight
103	  padded ones; on a place, the photographs set the count (`sections.md`).
104	- **Counts follow the content:** four real features are four cards, one quote is one quote, two plans
105	  are two plans. Zero testimonials is a normal page.
106	- **Find the organising idea** when the brief has one: the menu as the page, a timetable, a founder's
107	  letter, one object carried through every section. Let it break the template once.
108	- **Not the skeleton:** eyebrow, claim heading, two-line lede, three cards, figures, in every section.
109	  Vary what goes in the sections: a list, a table, a short letter, one longer paragraph (five lines
110	  at most, `copy.md`), a heading with one line under it.
111	
112	## 4. Draft
113	
114	Read `copy-moves.md` before drafting a whole page.
115	
116	- **Facts where adjectives want to go.** "Fast" is followed within the sentence by the figure or the
117	  mechanism; adjectives that stay are physical or measurable (wood-fired, 58 mm, ground-floor).
118	- **Proper nouns over categories:** the tools by name, the street, the river, the bus line.
119	- **The mechanism in verb-led steps.** How it works persuades more than how good it is.
120	- **The pain in the customer's words,** before the product, when the brief gives them.
121	- **One admission a page,** said plainly, from the brief.
122	- **Proof beside its claim,** from named outsiders the brief gives. No proof: a strip of plain facts
123	  from the brief, or nothing (`copy.md`).
124	- **Numbers in sentences, with their unit,** uneven where real.
125	- **Buttons:** a verb and the real object (`copy.md` rule 4). A true risk reversal sits beside the
126	  button ("Free for 14 days, no card"), only when the brief gives it.
127	- **Microcopy carries the voice too:** form labels and errors, the sent message, empty states, the 404
128	  page, the newsletter confirmation, a cookie notice if the page needs one. Write them in the register;
129	  this is where a dry line is welcome.
130	- **Sentence length follows meaning.** A short sentence lands a point; a long one carries an
131	  explanation. Not every line punchy; not variety by rule either.
132	- **Repeat the product's name** rather than cycling through "the platform, the tool, the solution".
133	
134	## 5. The device budget, per page
135	
136	None of these is banned; each works once. The problem is using them by default. `copy-lint.mjs`
137	counts them: over the budget is a WARN, twice the budget plus one or more is a FAIL (a tic).
138	
139	| Device | Budget | Note |
140	| --- | --- | --- |
141	| Heading in two fragments "X. Y." | 1 | spend it where it lands hardest |
142	| Number-pair heading "Four X, one Y" | 0 to 1 | the most repeated model habit |
143	| Negation run "No X. No Y." | 1 | only when each item is a refusal a buyer can check |
144	| Contrast "X, not Y", isn't, rather than, instead of, without the | 2 in all | banning one form moves you to the next; count them together |
145	| Dry closing line on a paragraph | 2, never in a row | most paragraphs end on information |
146	| Pun on the name or its metaphor | 1, never the h1 | it is the page's one brand line (`copy.md` rule 3) |
147	| Sign-off line in the footer | 0 | the footer holds facts (`copy.md`) |
148	| Strip of figures | facts from the brief only | never invented KPIs |
149	| Virtue words about ourselves | 0 | the lint skips literal ones (a quiet room, calm water, genuine parts) and allows 2 |
150	| Lists of three | when there are three things | never in consecutive sentences |
151	| Step numbers on cards | only where the order is the content (a booking's steps) | none on features that read in any order |
152	| Eyebrow labels | 1 or 2 a page | a heading that names the thing needs none |
153	| Testimonials | the brief's only | name and role or town; none is fine |
154	| Response-time promise | 1, from the brief | the same words wherever it repeats |
155	| "Since [year]" | 1, from the brief | |
156	
157	## 6. Check
158	
159	At step 6, before the gate (which runs the lint again):
160	
161	1. **Lint:** `node <skill>/scripts/copy-lint.mjs index.html --kind <kind>`. Fix every FAIL. Fix each
162	   WARN, or keep it on purpose and say why in the report.
163	2. **A rival's name:** put a rival's name, or the same trade in another town, into the h1, the sub-line
164	   and each heading. A line that still reads true says nothing about this client: rewrite it from the
165	   fact sheet.
166	3. **Sameness across pages:** when this session built other pages, pass them all to `copy-lint.mjs`
167	   at once and read the first headings side by side, and the heading phrases they share. A shared
168	   cadence or joke is a tic: break it.
169	4. **Read it aloud, as the client.** Cut every sentence they would not say about themselves.
170	5. **Over-correction:** after the fixes, look for the habit that replaced the one you removed: "rather
171	   than" multiplying, every sentence a fragment, everything in pairs, a joke deleted and nothing in its
172	   place. A rule that made a sentence worse is broken on purpose.
173	6. **A fresh reader,** when the run can spare a subagent: give it only the page's text and ask what
174	   this is, who it is for, why this over the alternative, what it costs, what would make it hesitate,
175	   and which three lines sound like any other website. Fix what it finds. Never iterate to beat an AI
176	   detector.
177	
178	The report carries the voice card in one line, every assumed price or hour (`copy.md`), and what the
179	client must supply.
