result.output:
## What every recipe assumes - **Frame.** `system.css` at 1440: `.wrap` 1280 at x 80 (a place 1200 at x 120), gutter 24, h1 72, h2 48; at 390: 342 at x 24. Every section is one or two screens, its h2 first, `--padt` under its top (`layout-v4.md`). Never add a number the system lacks; a missing value becomes a token. - **Splits** are the page's one split pair, text left and the visual right, top-aligned (`.grid`, never `.grid--middle` on a split), never mirrored; on a phone text first. - **Cards.** `cards.md` builds the card, its panel, the ground and the UI on it, and wins over anything here except the depth rule: two boxes at most. A card whose panel holds UI is `.card--open` (no box: its words on the page ground, the panel under them with four round corners) or runs its panel flush (`.panel--flush`); an inset panel holds only a picture. From 640 to 1023 a card with a panel takes the full row; from 1024 to 1279 span-4 cards with a panel go two-up, so a span-4 panel is never under 304px. - **Grounds in frames (tech).** The page has one effect and one card group's still grounds (`effects-usage.md`). Where a recipe below says "the card ground", it means that group's dealt id with its own seed per panel; "the effect" means the page's one effect, only in the hero or the one `[data-visual]` frame. Every other frame takes the lit ground plain (`.frame--lit`), a flat `--g-alt` panel, a photograph or a diagram. Product, service and place frames hold photographs on flat colour: never a code ground. - **Fragments** are pasted from `assets/ui//fragment.html` into their slot and rewritten: every name, number, subject, app and logo becomes the client's (`data-ui-load` shows the kit's sample text: drafts only). They sit in a `.stage` at their true size (`meta.json` `size`, `fluid`), never scaled, at the place the recipe names (else `meta.json`'s `place`). A `.fit` slot takes only a fragment whose minimum width fits it (`cards.md`): 324 in a 2x2 card at 1024, 256 in a span-4 card. The edge rule (every edge 24px clear, or cut by 24px or more with a fade) holds at 1440, 1280, 1024 and 768; move `--ax`/`--ay` until it does. On the phone cards.css places each fragment 16px in, its top at `--ay-sm` (24px unless set). - **Motion.** Fragments hold their finished picture; the one loop of a card group, split or wide frame carries `data-ui-loop` and its pause button; below the hero two loops are never on one screen; nothing moves because the page scrolled. Every timing: `motion.md`. Other kinds: no loops. - **Classes.** Only the system's, cards.css's and the kit's. Where a recipe needs one more rule it says "page CSS"; that only ever sits inside a visual, plus a place's visit panel (`sections.md` section 4). - **Photographs** lead every main section of a product, place or service page: the client's own, else picked with `photos.mjs` (`photos.md`), one look, shown plain, credited in the one footer line. No caption, name, price or link line under a bare picture: a sold item's name and price sit inside its card's padding. - **Names** in the examples (Ferrow, Rotaro, Kestrow, Ledgewick, Clausewise, Fenn, Halden...) are invented to show the form. Copy how they are written, never the words. Proof, quotes, customers and figures come only from the brief (`copy.md`). - **Logo, buttons, links.** `.nav__logo` holds the client's SVG, else the dealt mark and the name (the same in the footer). Buttons take the dealt look from ``; the nav's main action is `.btn.btn--primary` at the one button height (`system.md` Nav). Nav words, buttons and footer links go to `#ids`, the logo to `#top`, Contact to `#contact`; Privacy and Imprint to pages you write, or left out. # Navigation All four share the bar in `system.md`: fixed, opaque, 72px (56 on a phone), a 1px hairline, the same at every depth; a panel opens after 150ms of hover with a fade and a 6px drop, a click on the word goes to its section, never `preventDefault`. system.js adds the phone sheet, Esc and `aria-expanded`; never write a second handler. ## nav-centre **Job and use.** The quietest bar: the words in the middle of the bar, the logo on the left line, the main action on the right line. Software and services with four or five plain words. **At 1440.** `header.nav.nav--centre`: system.css centres the `.nav__links` group on the page axis; the logo and actions keep the `.wrap` lines. Four or five words, never wrapping at 1024. Menus as nav-mega's small menus. **At 390.** The logo left, the toggle right; the system's sheet. **Mistakes.** A group so wide it touches the logo or the button at 1024; a second row. ## bento **Job and use.** One main feature large and four small. Software with one lead feature, or a product with real photographs of its main part and four details. **At 1440.** `.grid`: row one `article.card.card--row.span-8` and `.span-4`, row two three `.span-4`. Every card: title, two lines in ink, then the panel, two boxes deep as in features-2x2, one `--p-h` for the group (336px). Wide card: `window` `.at-corner` (40/48, cut by the right and bottom, `.stage--fade-br`), or `files` `.at-corner.wide` (`--w: 680px`). Small cards (panel 347 at 1440, a `.fit` slot of 256): one fragment cut by the bottom: one that narrows to 256 centred `.at-rise.fit` (`chat`, `search` with `.to-edge`, a short stack low); `toggles` `.at-right.to-edge`; or a wider one (`stat`, `notify`, `cursor`) at its true width `.at-corner` (`--ax: 24px; --ay: 40px`), cut by the right and bottom. A `voice` call goes where its `meta.json` says and is then the group's loop. **At 1024 to 1279.** The wide card across the row, the four small ones two by two. **At 768 and 390.** One card per row. **Copy.** Wide card: the main feature as a verb and an object; small ones 2 to 4 words. Example, Ledgewick (bookkeeping for freelance designers): "Reads every receipt" / "Drop in PDFs or phone photos. The date, amount and VAT are filled in."; small: "Matches bank payments", "Tracks VAT", "Sends invoices", "Exports for your accountant". **Visual.** As features-2x2. A product: photographs in every panel, one look. **Motion.** Tech: the wide card loops; the four small ones hold still. Never two loops in one bento. **Mistakes.** Text in different places on different cards; small-card copy over two lines; `calendar`, `doc` or `code` in a small card; a bento next to another card grid. ## split-text-left **Job and use.** One thing the product does, in a few sentences and three facts, beside a picture that shows exactly that. The workhorse for software, products and studios. **At 1440.** `.grid`, top-aligned: the text on `span-5` (h2; 24px; two or three sentences at 20px; 24px; up to three short facts as plain lines; 24px; one `.link`) and `.frame.frame--split.span-6.start-7` (5:4, square on a phone) holding a `.stage.stage--fade-br`. The main piece is cut by the bottom, never floating with ground on all four sides: - `window` or the client's screenshot `.at-corner.to-edge` at `--ax`/`--ay` 56px, cut by the right and bottom; `files` the same with `.wide` (`--w: 680px`); - a narrower piece (`doc`, `code`, `chat`, `search`, `checklist`) `.at-rise.to-edge`, centred by `--w` and 56px down; a short one (`slider`, `toggles`) `.at-rise.fit` 40px down, cut below its second row. One small piece that shows the result (`cursor`, `notify`) only over a `window` or screenshot: `.at-over` its lower-right edge (`--bx: 24px; --by: -40px`), never over its first rows (Figma's panel with a small card over the product UI). A product or service: the frame holds the photograph of the part or the work the text names (`.frame--photo`, 628x471), never UI. **At 1024 to 1279.** The frame is 436 to 564 wide: the main piece alone. **At 768 and 390.** Text first, the frame 48px below, full width. **Copy.** Heading: the job and its result. Sentences in the order the picture plays. Example, Clausewise (contract review for small law firms): "Finds risky clauses in contracts"; "Upload a contract and every clause is checked against your firm's playbook."; link "See how review works"; `doc` rising out of the bottom with "unlimited liability" marked. **Visual.** Tech: the effect when this frame is the page's `[data-visual]`, else the lit ground plain. The main piece shows the text step for step; the small one shows what comes out. **Motion.** Tech: one loop, in the small piece or the main one. **Mistakes.** Text and frame not top-aligned; a four-line h2; a picture that shows something the text does not say; a button pair instead of one link; a second split on the other side. ## app-frame **Job and use.** The product itself, big, the way Linear, Cursor and Vercel show it: one real app window across the `.wrap`, the list beside the open item, the app's own chrome. Every software page has one, in the hero or within the first three sections (in testing: a code-review page whose review was one small diff card centred on a sage panel scored about 3.5 points under Linear, whose review band puts the pull-request list beside a full-width diff in one app frame). Never on gaming, product, service or place. **The two panes** (kit fragments, rewritten to the client's names; the list is always `window`): | Product | List pane | Open pane | |---|---|---| | Code review | `window`: pull requests | `diff-review` (the comment and Apply in its top 250px) | | Support, inbox, CRM, agents | `window`: conversations | `chat` (the open thread) | | Docs, contracts, knowledge | `window`: documents | `doc` (the page with its marked phrase) | | CI, deploys | `window`: runs | `pipeline-board` (wide: nodes and log) or `terminal-run` | | Booking, scheduling | `window`: bookings | `calendar` | The `window`'s rows: `.ui-win__who` the person (author, customer, owner), `.ui-win__sub` the item and its detail ("Retry settle jobs · +4 −3"), the status chip the product's own states (`data-open`, `data-work`, `data-done`), sidebar labels one word each. Write 9 or more rows and enough lines in the open item (24 or more for a diff) that both panes run past the frame's bottom: the frame cuts them under its fade, never an empty strip of pane under the last row. **At 1440.** One screen. `.grid`, top-aligned: the h2 on `span-5`, a grey paragraph (about 25 words) with one `.link` on `span-6 start-7`. 48px below, the frame takes the rest of the screen as `.fill` (about 1280 x 550): ```html
[window fragment]
[the open item's fragment]
``` `class="ui"` gives the frame the kit's tokens, and tells the checks it is one drawn window. Page CSS (the whole recipe): ```css .app.ui { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 5fr) minmax(0, 7fr); margin-top: var(--s-7); background: var(--u-bg); border: 1px solid var(--u-border); border-radius: var(--u-r); box-shadow: var(--u-shadow); } .app > .app__pane { position: relative; min-width: 0; min-height: 0; overflow: hidden; } .app > .app__pane + .app__pane { border-left: 1px solid var(--u-line); } .app > .app__pane > .ui-panel { width: 100%; border: 0; border-radius: 0; box-shadow: none; } .app > .app__pane::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: auto 0 0 0; height: 64px; background: linear-gradient(transparent, var(--u-bg)); pointer-events: none; } @media (min-width: 1024px) and (max-width: 1279px) { .app.ui { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 4fr) minmax(0, 8fr); } } @media (max-width: 1023px) { .app.ui { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0, 1fr); } .app > .app__pane--list { max-height: 252px; } .app > .app__pane--list::after { display: none; } .app .ui-win__side { display: none; } .app .ui-win__body { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); } .app > .app__pane + .app__pane { border-left: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--u-line); } } @media (max-width: 639px) { .app.ui { grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr); } .app > .app__pane--list { display: none; } .app > .app__pane + .app__pane { border-top: 0; } } ``` The `window` lays itself out for its pane (rows stacked name over item at 1440, columns on a tablet). The fragments keep their natural height: the pane cuts them, never their own box. One box: the frame is the window, the panes are its columns, no panel, card or ground behind it (it sits on the section's ground; on a `dark-band` the kit's dark surface). A second piece over it (`cursor`, `notify`) only `.at-over` the open pane's lower-right, never over the list. **At 1024 to 1279.** The list narrows to 4 columns (its sidebar goes); the open item takes 8. **At 768 to 1023.** The list on top (its bar, column heads and four whole rows, 252px), the open item under it to the section's foot. **At 390.** The open item alone, its own header as the chrome. **Copy.** The h2 names what the window shows ("Every pull request, reviewed in one place"); the paragraph says the steps in the order the window shows them. **Motion.** One loop: the open item (`data-ui-loop` on its pane: the Apply pressed, the answer written); the list holds still. Nothing scrolls inside the window. **Mistakes.** The open item alone on a lit panel (that is a card, not the product); the list and the item as two boxes side by side with ground between; a pane that ends in empty white; the kit's sample rows; a fragment stretched to the pane's height (its own overflow then cuts its text). ## steps **Job and use.** How the product is used, in order, each step's result shown. Only with three real steps. **At 1440.** `.section-head`, then `.grid` with three `article.card.card--row.span-4`: `span.step-num`, the title (a verb and an object, one line), one or two lines in ink, then the panel, two boxes deep (336px; a service: a photograph of the step fills it), with one fragment placed as in the bento's small cards. Not `calendar`, `files`, `doc` or `cursor`. No arrows or lines between the cards. **At 1024 to 1279.** Two cards, then the third across the row. **At 768 and 390.** One column. **Copy.** The heading holds the count. Example, Ledgewick: "Set up Ledgewick in 3 steps"; "Upload your receipts" / "Drop in PDFs or phone photos."; "Check the matches" / "You confirm the few it is unsure about." **Motion.** Tech: the first card loops; the others hold still. Never chained or staggered. **Mistakes.** Arrows or stair-stepped cards; huge display numerals; panels of different heights. # Photographs, rooms, services and people ## faq **Job and use.** The buyer's last questions (price, data, cancelling, formats), every answer open. Merged into the section above under 495px. **At 1440.** The page's split: on the left the h2 "Questions", a grey line and a `.link` to `#contact` (a `mailto:` or `tel:` only with an address or number the brief gives); on the right `.faq` with 5 to 8 `.faq__item`s (the question in `h3`, the answer under it, each closed by a 1px rule). No accordion: answers are open on load. **At 390.** One column. **Copy.** Questions in the buyer's words, at most 60 characters; answers under 50 words, starting with the answer. Example, Ferrow: "Can I cancel at any time?" "Yes. Cancel in Settings and you are not billed again." **Mistakes.** Questions the company wants asked; answers that dodge; closed answers. # Closes The close is row 1 of `footer.closing` (`layout-v4.md`), on the footer's own ground, never a band of its own. It asks for the main action once more, word for word. ## close-type **Job and use.** One big line and one big primary button. Any kind; no picture: the button is the picture. **At 1440.** `.closing__cta.close--type`: the h2 (at most eight words, on the left line), an optional `.t-small.muted` line (the trial terms, the opening hours), then `a.btn.btn--primary.btn--xl` across the `.wrap` (88px tall, its label in the display face at 32px) on software, 640 wide and 72 tall on product and service (a slab that wide reads blunt on a clinic). **At 390.** The button full width, 48px tall with an 18px label. **Copy.** Example, Rotaro: "Plan next week's rota in ten minutes" / "Start free trial" / "Free for 14 days. No card needed." **Mistakes.** A second button; the big button anywhere else on the page; a ground behind it. ## footer-dark **Job and use.** Figma's and x.ai's footer: a dark ground, the name set large, the link columns. # Moments

A moment is the award-site part of a page (house rule 8): the one place, or two, where a page does
something a visitor remembers, in a section of its own; besides it the page has only the hero's
entrance and the hover layer (`motion.md`, The rule). Each is a folder in `assets/moments/<id>/`
(`moment.js`, `moment.css`, `meta.json`, a full `demo.html`); `index.json` lists them,
`gallery.html` links the demos and `moments.js` runs them. Eighteen folders: five retired
(`headline-arrives`, `closing-lift`, `lines-rise`, `window-parallax`, `word-rotate`), and thirteen
dealt by kind (below).

**Which pages: every page.** One moment on a short page, two on a long one (eight sections or more,
in two different sections), never three, on every kind. The place's short page (under 8
photographs, `sections.md` section 4) skips the type moment: its one moment is `picture-develops`
on the section's photograph (`--fits section --photo`, dealt again with `--exclude photo-chapters`
when it gives `photo-chapters`), or, with no photograph, `word-highlight` in a one-screen statement
section of its own, so the page is four screens.

| page kind | dealt from | look |
|---|---|---|
| place (cafe, bakery, guesthouse, shop, gym; a studio with a door is passed as `--page place`, since `--page studio` reads as service) | `photo-chapters`, `picture-develops` (film), `word-highlight` | photographs and type |
| product (site-kind other) | `photo-chapters`, `pinned-chapters`, `picture-develops` (film), `word-highlight` | photographs and type |
| service (firm, clinic, agency, trade) | `photo-chapters`, `pinned-chapters`, `picture-develops` (film), `word-highlight` | photographs and type |
| software, gaming, tech | the eleven that list them: every dealt moment but `photo-chapters` and `picture-develops` | as before 2.5.1 |

Why these for the other kinds: each is led by the client's own photographs or words, moves only in
its own section, costs no WebGL and reads as calm (a hotel, a law firm, a wedding photographer). Not
on them: anything with a shader, WebGL or a liquid or pointer effect (`liquid-hover`,
`liquid-type`, `cursor-spotlight`), anything that reads as a graphic trick (`iris-opens`,
`line-carries-colour`, `letters-assemble`, the halftone of `picture-develops`, and
`giant-type-pass`: a photograph inside letters reads as a template trick, muddies a warm palette
and is a parallax), a loop (`marquee-row`) and a count (`counter-rolls`). On those
pages the two of a long page are the statement moment (`word-highlight`) and one section moment
(the photographs), or the photograph that develops beside one of the chapters moments (two kinds:
one runs once as it enters, the other follows the scroll). `photo-chapters` and `pinned-chapters` never share a page and do different
jobs: photo-chapters tells a story in full-width photographs with one chapter at a time on a panel;
pinned-chapters walks through steps listed beside one frame (how a booking or an order goes).

- **`--fits section,statement`:** a statement is a section of its own, so the letters, liquid type,

## The still rule (every moment, no exception)

Every moment has a static variant for a **phone** and for **reduced motion**, and a finished state
without script or when its module fails. The loader decides: it hands each moment a `lib` whose
`reduced()` answers `lib.still()`, which is true under `prefers-reduced-motion` and on a phone (under
640px wide, or a touch screen turned sideways under 500px tall). A moment written against `reduced()`
therefore shows its finished state there, and the host carries `data-moment-still="reduced"`,
`"phone"` or `"card"`. **Phones still get a moment:** the ones light enough for a phone (one
picture or one paragraph at a time; transform, clip, filter or colour) say `export const phone =
true` in their `moment.js` and `"phoneRuns": true` in `meta.json`, and run there; only reduced
motion and a card keep them still. Those are `word-highlight`, `picture-develops` (film) and
`photo-chapters` (from 600px of height), which covers every place, product and service deal. The answer is taken when the moment mounts (a window resized across 640px

still shows (`reduced`, `phone`). Hover moments do nothing on touch screens either.

**Nothing on a card moves on scroll** (house rule). A moment sits on a hero, a statement, one
section, a transition or the close, never in a card, a plan, a result or a bento cell: the loader
leaves one that does still (`data-moment-still="card"`, `data-moments-card` on `<html>`) and
`moments.mjs check` calls it a fault.

## Put one on the page

The host is a section of the page (or, for the text moments, the headline or the row inside it);
mark it as the moment's header comment shows (`data-moment="<id>"`, options in `data-moment-opts`).
Every section stays one or two screens tall (`layout-v4.md`, `--h`), live and at rest, but the two
chapters moments: `photo-chapters` is (hold + 1) screens live (three for three chapters, four for
four or five; write no `--h` and no `data-screen` on it: the checker and the layout check both read a
live photo-chapters section as whole screens, four at most) and both are as tall as their content at rest. A transition's
host is the whole section that sits on the new ground, a statement moment is one section with its h2
first, a marquee or counter row merges into the section above as its last row. In `<head>`, the one line plus a `modulepreload` for
the loader, its lib and the dealt moment:

```html
<script>document.documentElement.classList.add('mo-js');setTimeout(()=>document.documentElement.classList.add('mo-safe'),2500)</script>
<link rel="modulepreload" href="assets/moments/moments.js"><link rel="modulepreload" href="assets/moments/lib.js"><link rel="modulepreload" href="assets/moments/<id>/moment.js">
```

Then the loader once. On a page with `system.js`, `system.js` imports it and waits for it. On a page
without, the demo pages' tag at the end of `<body>`:

```html
<script type="module" src="assets/moments/moments.js"></script>
```

The loader links each moment's CSS and starts it; `<html data-moments-ready>` says when. A failed
module gets `data-moment-failed` and the class `mo-safe` on its own element, which the moment's CSS
reads as "show the finished state now". A demo's copy and photographs are placeholders. Every moment
takes the page's tokens (`--bg`, `--ink`, `--muted`, `--accent`, `--line`, the display face).

A moment's section in a page is copied from one of the two page models, which mount moments inside
a starter page and pass the checker: `assets/moments/_demo/in-page.html` (a place:
`photo-chapters`, `word-highlight`) and `in-page-service.html` (a service: `pinned-chapters`,
`picture-develops` in its film look). A moment's own `demo.html` shows it alone and is not a page
model.

## Rules

- **The kind's count, an id once.** `data-moments-over` and `data-moments-repeat` on `<html>` are faults.
- **No random effects as you scroll.** A scroll moment is scrubbed to the scrollbar inside its own
  section, which stays one or two screens tall (`photo-chapters` three or four), and does one purposeful thing; at the section's top
  and bottom it shows a finished state (every transition and `letters-assemble` finish before the
  section's top is a fifth of the screen down), so each judge tile shows one whole section. No card,
  row or tile ever enters on scroll. `consistency.mjs` reports a scroll finding inside the dealt
  `[data-moment]` section; that one is expected, any other is a fault.
- **Content is readable without the motion:** the words are in the HTML, in their finished place; a
  moment never hides a headline on load (the hero's own entrance is the motion layer's, `motion.md`).
- **Photo-led on the other kinds:** a place, product or service page's moment carries the client's
  own photographs (or library ones that pass `photos.md`), each used once on the page, and its
  words are the page's real copy; never a stand-in picture to give the moment something to move.
- **One count a page:** `counter-rolls` or `data-m-count` (`motion.md`), never both.
- **Nothing blinks, bounces or overshoots.** Ease-outs (cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) for a settle),
  600-1,000 ms for a reveal, 1.6-1.8 s for a photograph developing; a scrubbed wipe or change takes
  about half of its chapter's share of the scroll and holds for the rest; a loop runs its rounds and
  rests, or carries a pause button.
- **The page's edges.** A moment's text sits in a `.container` or `.wrap` like every other section: its
  words end on the page's left and right edges. A transition's cover is an inset panel inside the host
  section with an even gutter on every side (card corners, never touching the section's edges), its
  line or ring inside the panel; every heading, paragraph, button and picture appears whole, never cut
  by the line or the disc (each moment's `meta.json`, `look`, says how).
- **Cost:** no WebGL but `liquid-hover` (tech only) (one context, only near the screen; a plain photograph without
  WebGL or when the shader fails). `liquid-type` is one SVG filter on one headline, on only while a
  ripple is alive. Every other moment costs CSS variables, a transform or a clip and a passive
  listener.
- **One pointer effect a page:** a hover or liquid moment rules out `fx-button`, `fx-spotlight` and an
  object that turns to the pointer, and the reverse; `pick` never deals two of them.
- **Photographs:** `giant-type-pass` and `liquid-hover` (tech) want mid to dark tones with edges and detail; a
  pale dusk sky reads lavender in a letter and a flat sea shows no ripple. Never violet or lavender.
- **No captions;** the photograph's credit goes in the footer line.

# Effects usage

Who gets effects, how many, how they are dealt and where they sit. An effect is anything a shader,
canvas, WebGL, a print pass or a scroll drive makes: effect grounds (`data-fx`, `assets/effects`),
the WebGL creative parts (`effects-creative.md`), objects and prints (`effects-objects.md`), big
scenes (`scenes.md`), the tech moments (`moments.md`; the photo- and type-led ones every kind deals
are not effects), a film or 3D hero and timed loops. `cards.md` wins on
any card detail; `motion.md` holds every timing.

## The gate (house rule 8)

Effects are for site-kind tech, software and gaming (AI and developer tools count as software) and
for a product page with a technical subject (hardware, devices). Never on a place, an ordinary
product brand or shop, a service firm, an agency or a studio: they are site-kind other.

On other, photographs, type and flat colour carry the page. Banned there: canvas and WebGL, autoplay
video, any CSS gradient (grounds, panels, glows, scrims), SVG pattern or texture grounds,
`backdrop-filter` (the nav too), `filter`, `mix-blend-mode`, `mask-image`, glass, grain, halftone,
dither, duotone, print, `[data-fx]`, `[data-print]`, `[data-scene]`, `[data-big-scene]`,
`[data-ui-loop]`, `[data-m-loop]`, `[data-m-count]`, SVG animation, GIFs, Lottie, a
custom cursor and any scroll or animation library. Allowed: the hero's entrance and the one or two
dealt photo- or type-led moments (`photo-chapters`, `pinned-chapters`, `picture-develops` in its
film look, `word-highlight`: `moments.md`), `fx-map` baked still, `fx-photo` as a
plain photograph, real icons, a still diagram (not on a place), and on a physical product whose
brief asks for 3D its own product render (`[data-product]`, `effects-objects.md`): the product's
picture, not an effect: stills by default, live only when asked (`data-product-mode="live"`), at
most one live context, on the flat ground, its poster beneath. Without that ask a product with no
photographs is shown in stand-in photographs (`photos.md`).

## What each kind gets

| | tech | product, service (other) | place |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lead picture | the client's UI (hardware: its photographs or CAD render, else stand-in photographs of its kind, never an effect or an order form alone; a game: its name and its art, else its name over a stand-in photograph of its setting; a render only when the brief asks for 3D) | its photographs; a product without them: stand-in photographs of its kind (a render only when the brief asks for 3D) | its photographs (a remote place: its region's landscape) |
| The one effect | a live ground, a WebGL part, an object or a big scene | none | none |
| Card panel grounds | one card group, still, from the effect's family; with a big scene the lit ground (`data-ground`), no `data-fx` | the client's photograph | none |
| Moments | 1 or 2 a page, two at most in all: in sections, one of them may sit in the hero | 1 or 2 in sections, photo- or type-led (`moments.md`) | 1 or 2 in sections, photo- or type-led (`moments.md`) |
| Big scene | 0 or 1 (it is the effect) | none | none |
| Diagram cards | 0 to 2, pulsing | 0 or 1, still | none |
| Loops | one timed loop, one per card group | none | none |
| CSS grounds | 0 to 2 (`backgrounds.md`) | flat tokens | flat tokens |

**The subject before the effect** (in testing: a robot arm shown as a silk shader and an order form,
and an unnamed game shown as an abstract effect, both lost to pages that showed the thing). An
effect never stands where the product, the device or the game's world should be. Hardware with no
photographs or client renders takes stand-in photographs of the same kind of machine at work, and
a game with no art files its name set large over stand-in photographs of its setting (`photos.md`,
Live search; `sections.md`, Product and Gaming), full bleed in the world section. When the brief

content.text:
`/about` is rebuilt with the taste skill as a standalone static page and pushed to main (`3f188a9`). The app screens are unchanged.

**The skill's finish gate did not run.** You asked me not to use its headless Chrome scripts, so I measured the page myself in Chrome, in 1440×900, 768×1024 and 390×844 frames. The skill's copy-lint (no browser) passes with 0 FAIL and 0 WARN on 569 words. Type check, lint and the 61 app tests pass.

**How it's built**
- It's `frontend/public/about.html`, and a rewrite in `next.config.ts` serves it at `/about`. The kit's own CSS takes over the page's body, sections, header and footer, so it couldn't sit inside the app's layout without breaking the app pages.
- `public/assets/` holds only the kit parts the page loads (1.9 MB).
- The old `Landing.tsx`, its route and its CSS are deleted, and the app nav now links to `/about` with a plain link.

**What the skill dealt** (picked at random, as it requires)
- **Hero:** a centred headline over a product window, with the aurora-curtains effect, given the page's teal colours, behind it. The first effect it offered, gradient-mesh, rendered black.
- **Colours and type:** an off-white and slate palette with a teal accent; Instrument Sans for text and DM Mono for figures.
- **Page parts:** centred nav, pill buttons, arc logo mark, one big closing button, and a dark footer.
- **Two moments:** the headline "Know who to skip before Slush." ripples under the cursor, and the flip section opens through a widening circle as you scroll to it.

**The page, top to bottom**
1. Hero: "Investor screening for founders", with Sensofusion's 9 to skip and 26 to pitch as the opening fact.
2. The founder report as a full window: the investor list beside Skyfall's open conflict with its sources.
3. The statement, with a row of real facts from Sensofusion's report under it.
4. The investor check, from the fund's side.
5. How a report is built, in 3 steps.
6. Slush briefs, and answers from your own agent (MCP).
7. Questions.
8. The close and footer.

Every name, number, date and reason comes from the live Sensofusion report or `PRODUCT.md`. Two things I'd first written myself were corrected from the data: a competitor reason that wasn't the one Gemini actually gave, and an industry Cala doesn't list.

**What I measured**
- Every section is exactly one or two screens at all three sizes, with its heading 120 px from the top on desktop.
- Nothing scrolls sideways, and at 1440×900 all content ends inside its screen.
- I fixed what the checks turned up: an FAQ that ran long, sections set to two screens on phone and tablet, an empty-looking statement screen, a citation the page flagged as a leftover placeholder, and a badge cut off on phones.

**Not checked**
- Performance, the 320 px width, real touch, and whether the two moments run correctly.
- At 768 and 1440 the footer links are 19 px tall, the kit's own footer styling; the skill's tap-size check may flag them.

**Things to know**
- **The deployed `/about` shows the old landing page** until A redeploys from main.
- **There's no share picture** (`og:image`): the skill makes one with its headless screenshot script. The canonical link waits for a real domain.
- **This page has its own look.** It uses the skill's palette and fonts, not DESIGN.md's, so it no longer matches the app screens. That's the trade-off of choosing a full redesign.
- **Uncommitted:** `frontend/.taste-skill/` holds the skill's deal history; you can delete it or add it to `.gitignore`.

+  (`tests/xray_off.py`, autouse in B's test folders).
+
+## B23 Pitch this week: fresh funds + the partner (14 Nov, for C and the demo script)
+
+- **(a) Fresh funds:** Cala's search asks which VC firms closed a fund for the startup's sector
+  this year or last; Gemini only copies firm names out of the cited claims (a name that is not
+  in its claim word for word is dropped), each is resolved to a Cala investor. They join the
+  Pitch pool; reason "Fresh fund: <the claim>" with its sources; activity counts full ("activity
+  10/10 (fresh fund for your sector)"). Aerospace and defence today: Lakestar (Resilience I,
+  €262M, Jul 2026), Earlybird + AVP (E2D, €500M), Expansion Ventures (€137M). Stored per sector.
+- **Sector:** the startup's industry tag, else the tag most of its competitors and space share
+  (Sensofusion has none in Cala: "aerospace and defense").
+- **(b) The partner:** for the top 5 Pitch investors, "Partner for your space: <name>. <claim>"
+  with sources (Maki.vc: Paavo Räisänen, Gungnir: Max Villman, Lakestar: Simon King; none found
+  for NIF, Lifeline, Tesi in this sector). Stored per investor and sector, also "none".
+  The name is matched against every direct competitor's BOARD members: a match is a `BOARD`
+  conflict (`via_person` = the board member) → Skip, reason "Conflict: its partner X sits on
+  the board of Y, a direct competitor". None on the demo companies today. The investor check and
+  the agent's check_conflict apply a partner a report already found (no search there).
+- **Live tops (server after redeploy):** Sensofusion Maki.vc 69.6, NIF 38.0, Lifeline 36.3;
+  Kelluu: Lakestar is new at #4 (32.5). No contract change.
+- **Cost:** first report per sector ~1 min more (Cala search ~55 s), each new top investor
+  ~15-40 s once; then nothing (stored).
+
+## Contract 1.2.0 is on main: B24 notes + B25 sanctions (14 Nov, for C, please read)
+
+Agreed by the humans (A, B, C): one additive bump. CHANGELOG, api.md, CLAUDE.md §5 updated.

+- **For C, needed before a sanction can show correctly** (none on the demo companies today):
+  `frontend/lib/types.ts` (`ConflictKind` gains `"SANCTION"`, `FounderReport.notes`,
+  `CONTRACT_VERSION = "1.2.0"`), and `conflictText` in `lib/investor.ts`: today a SANCTION
+  conflict would read "Backed your competitor <X>". For SANCTION, `competitor` is **the
+  sanctioned entity** (the fund itself or its LP); suggested text: "Sanctions record in Cala on
+  <X>" (+ "its LP" when X is not the investor). Same for the Skip roll call and the check.
+- **B25 Sanctions screen:** every ranked investor and up to 5 LPs each, against Cala's
+  `IS_SUBJECT_OF_SANCTION` (ID-based, sourced, e.g. Rosoboronexport → "Sanctioned: EU.7808.66

+  has a sanctions record in Cala: …". No hit = the reason **"screened: no sanctions record in
+  Cala"** (exact; C shows it as a plain line). Cala trouble = neither (not screened). Also in
+  the investor check, briefs and the agent's check_conflict. Live: 153 investors screened on the

+- **B24 Notes:** `FounderReport.notes` = sourced lines on the direct competitors.
+  "Non-dilutive: <claim>" for grants they won (one Cala search naming them: NATO DIANA, EDF,
+  EIC, national programmes); "At Slush 2026: <claim>" for rivals that attend (none found

The pull brought in contract 1.2.0, and I've updated the frontend and the demo script to match. Both commits are pushed (`e505acf`, `9c3b585`). Tests (69), lint, the type check and the build all pass. I checked the founder report in Chrome against the deployed API, which now reports 1.2.0.

**What came in:** B finished B22 to B25.
- **B22:** a portfolio check that finds rivals not on the competitor list.
- **B23:** funds that just closed a fund for the sector, plus the partner to approach.
- **B24:** grants the competitors won.
- **B25:** a sanctions screen.

All three humans agreed to contract 1.2.0. It adds the `SANCTION` conflict kind I asked about, and a list of notes on each founder report.

**Frontend changes:**
- **Sanctions:** a sanctions hit now names the fund itself or its LP, instead of reading "Backed your competitor …". This covers the Skip cards, the "Don't pitch these" list, the copied Skip list, the verdict line and the investor check. When a sanction is the only hit, the check's heading reads "Sanctions record."
- **"Screened: no sanctions record in Cala":** every investor now carries this line, so I moved it to the end of the reasons. Otherwise it takes one of the three visible slots on each card.
- **Grant notes:** these now show under the competitor chips as "Also about your competitors", with source badges. On Sensofusion they're Frankenburg's EU defence fund grant and MyDefence's grant from Innovation Fund Denmark.
- **Hidden rivals:** BSV Ventures is first on the Skip list for backing Zvook, which isn't one of the four competitor chips. The list now says "backed Zvook (a rival found in its portfolio)" so it doesn't look like an error.
- **Sample data:** the sample report and the mock keep sanctions when competitors are removed, since a sanction isn't tied to a competitor.

No demo company has a sanctions hit, so the sanctions wording is covered only by unit tests, not seen on a real page.

**Demo script:** the live numbers moved since the last version, so I updated it:
- Skip is now 11 (was 9) and Pitch is 30. BSV is first and Skyfall second.
- Maki.vc is 69.9, still shown as 70.
- The spoken lines now say "eleven funds" and mention BSV as a rival found in its portfolio.
- The script's click path still runs through Skyfall, so steps 4 to 7 are unchanged.

The local server is still running on port 3000 against the deployed API, in case you want to look.
